learning_outcomes.text: Student knows and understands the meaning of the fundamental notions of electroheat
Student has the present knowledge of the use of fundamental electroheat technologies in various industrial and domestic implementations as well as their importance
Student knows and understands the basic methods of electroheat, structures and properties of chosen electroheat equipment and their fields of applications
Student is able to present his own work containing the results of an experiment and their discussion
Student is able to determine the efficiency of electroheat equipment and assess the distribution of the generated temperature field
Student is able to cooperate with the group during measurements and formulate conclusions concerning the properties of the electroheat equipement being investigated

syllabus_topics: Introduction to electroheat. Fundamental notions and classification systems used in electroheat. Energy conversions in electroheat. Electrical, thermal and electrothermal efficiencies. Brief description of heating methods. Temperature measurements and control.

Resistance heating. Heating elements. Direct and indirect resistance electroheat installations. Heat characteristics of resistance furnaces. Industrial and domestic applications of resistance heating.
Infra-red heating. Infra-red installations and their applications.
Electrode heating. Electrode heating installations used for water heating, glass melting and metals remelting.
Arc heating. Arc furnaces. Determination of parameters of heavy-current carrying conductors. Electrode movement regulators.

Induction heating. Heating of conductive materials in medium- and high frequency electromagnetic field. Depth of penetration. Distribution of current density and volume power density in the charge. Induction heaters. Induction crucible furnaces and induction channel furnaces. Power supply of induction installations. Frequency changers. Applications of induction heating. Induction cookers.
Dielectric and microwave heating. Heating of dielectrics in high-frequency electromagnetic field. Dielectric heaters and furnaces. Microwave ovens.
Other methods and installations of electroheat. Safety in electroheat installations.
Microwave heating. Measurements of the model of an oven. Investigation of the temperature field and determination of the device efficiency in various loading conditions and for different materials.

Induction heating. Measurements of an induction cooker. Presentation of highfrequency generators. Simulation of operation of systems in various topologies and determination of parameters of the equivalent inductor-load circuit.

Regulation and registration of temperature. Temperature measurement methods (contact and contactless ways). Calibration of thermocouples. The use of programmable systems for the process temperature control.
Resistance heating – design of a resistance heating element for a resistance furnace.

Electrode heating – investigations of an electrode furnace model and determination of the device efficiency. Selection of the optimum operating point of the furnace for a variety of power conditions, the geometry of the electrodes and the conductivity of the heated liquid.

Infrared heating. Investigation of an infrared cooker. Determination of the efficiency of the device. Presentation of different technologies used in infrared devices. Determination of the percentage of conduction, radiation and convection in heat transfer.

Control of resistance heating devices – phase control and time proportional control (resistive and resistive-inductive loads). Testing and registration of the waveforms. Testing of operation of dedicated controllers: a microprocessor-based one (phase, time proportional control types) and phase controller built using an integrated circuit U2008.
assessment_rules: It is necessary to obtain positive Laboratory Grade (LG) and Lecture Test Grade (LTG). The weighted average (WAV) of both grades is calculated: WAV = 0.7 LG + 0.3 LTG. The final grade (FG) is determined based on the WAV: if WAV > 4.75 then FG = 5.0, else if WAV > 4.25 then FG = 4.5, else if WAV > 3.75 then FG = 4.0, else if WAV > 3.25 then FG = 3.5, else FG = 3. If positive grades LG and LTG were obtained in the first term and the calculated FG is less than 5.0, FG will be increased by 0.5 if the student has participated in at least 75% of lectures.
